target: İş arkadaşımla öğle yemeğinde buluşacağım.
english: I'll meet my colleague for lunch.
tip: The ending -la/-le means with: arkadaşımla = with my colleague, from arkadaşım plus la.

target: Bu kapıyı açabilir misiniz lütfen?
english: Can you open this door please?
tip: -abil- adds can, and as a question it becomes a polite request: açabilir misiniz = could you open.

target: Künefe taze peynirle yapıldığında harika oluyor.
english: Kunefe is wonderful when made with fresh cheese.
tip: -dığında means when something happens, attached to the verb: yapıldığında = when it is made.

target: O genellikle resim çizerdi çünkü zamanı vardı.
english: He usually drew pictures because he had time.
tip: The -erdi/-ardı ending is the habitual past, used to do: çizerdi = used to draw regularly.

target: Param olsa deniz kenarında bir ev alırdım.
english: If I had money, I would buy a house by the sea.
tip: Unreal wish: -sa on the condition, -irdim on the result. olsa ... alırdım = if I had ... I would buy.

target: Hükümet yeni reformlar yapmaktadır.
english: The government is making new reforms.
tip: -maktadır is a formal written present continuous, common in news: yapmaktadır = is making.

target: Ablası erkek kardeşinden daha uzun.
english: His older sister is taller than he is.
tip: Comparisons use ablative -den plus daha: kardeşinden daha uzun = taller than the brother.

target: Pencereden gördüğüm manzara çok güzeldi.
english: The view I saw from the window was very beautiful.
tip: -dığım builds a relative clause, the thing that I did: gördüğüm manzara = the view that I saw.

target: Spor salonuna haftada üç kez gidiyorum.
english: I go to the gym three times a week.
tip: Locative -da can mean per for frequency: haftada üç kez = three times a week.

target: Meydanda eski bir çeşme var, yüzyıllardır akıyor.
english: In the square there's an old fountain, flowing for centuries.
tip: Add -dır to a time span to mean for that long: yüzyıllardır = for centuries and still going.

target: Yolda cüzdanımı düşürdüm, biri bulup geri getirdi.
english: I dropped my wallet on the road, someone found it and brought it back.
tip: -ip chains two verbs with one subject, and only the last carries tense: bulup getirdi = found and brought.

target: Bu parkta sabahları spor yapan çok insan var.
english: There are many people exercising in this park in the mornings.
tip: -an turns a verb into the one who does it, before a noun: spor yapan insan = people who exercise.

target: Buzul erimeseydi kutup ayısının yaşam alanı daralmazdı.
english: If the glacier hadn't melted, the polar bear's habitat wouldn't have shrunk.
tip: Past what-if: -seydi on the condition, -mazdı result. erimeseydi ... daralmazdı = if it hadn't melted, wouldn't have shrunk.

target: Şehir hızla büyümektedir.
english: The city is growing rapidly.
tip: büyümektedir uses -mektedir, a formal written present continuous seen in news and reports. Everyday speech would just say büyüyor.

target: Beş yıldır burada yaşıyoruz.
english: We have been living here for five years.
tip: Beş yıldır keeps the present tense yaşıyoruz where English switches to have been living. The -dir on a time span means for that long.

target: Sağlığınıza dikkat etmezseniz hastalanırsınız.
english: If you don't pay attention to your health you'll get sick.
tip: etmezseniz stacks the negative aorist -mez onto the conditional -se: if you do not pay attention. The positive, ederseniz, means if you do.

target: Okul Eylül'de başlar, Haziran'da biter.
english: School starts in September and ends in June.
tip: başlar and biter use the aorist -r for timeless, habitual facts like a school calendar, not one event happening right now.

target: Çocuklara dikkat et, parkta koşuyorlar.
english: Watch the children, they're running in the park.
tip: dikkat etmek takes the dative: Çocuklara dikkat et, watch the children, uses -a, not the plain object form çocukları.

target: Bugün erken çıkarsak trafikten kurtuluruz.
english: If we leave early today we'll escape traffic.
tip: kurtulmak pairs with the ablative -ten: trafikten kurtuluruz, we get free from traffic, marks what you escape from.

target: Acele etme, hâlâ yeterince zamanımız var.
english: Don't rush, we still have enough time.
tip: etme is the singular do not: Acele etme to one person. For plural or polite address you would say etmeyin instead.

target: Işıkları söndür ve pencereyi kapat giderken.
english: Turn off the lights and close the window when you leave.
tip: -ken means while or as: giderken is as you leave, pinning one action to the moment of another.

target: Yeni komşularımız çok gürültücü, gece uyuyamıyorum.
english: Our new neighbors are very noisy, I can't sleep at night.
tip: uyuyamıyorum carries -ama, cannot: I am unable to sleep. Without it, uyumuyorum would just mean I am not sleeping.

target: Komşumuz her zaman çamaşır yıkar ama bir türlü bitiremez.
english: Our neighbor always washes laundry but can never finish it.
tip: bir türlü with a negative verb means no matter what, never: bir türlü bitiremez, she can never finish it.

target: Babam her zaman şarkı söylerdi çünkü canı sıkılırdı.
english: My dad always sang because he got bored.
tip: söylerdi is the aorist plus -di, the used-to past for a repeated habit, not one single occasion of singing.

target: Bu yemek tarifi internette çok popüler olmuş.
english: This recipe has become very popular on the internet.
tip: olmuş uses -miş, reporting something inferred or heard rather than personally witnessed: it has apparently become popular.

target: Bu formu doldurun ve masaya bırakın lütfen.
english: Fill out this form and leave it on the desk please.
tip: doldurun and bırakın take -un/-ın, the polite or plural command. To one person informally it is doldur and bırak.

target: Eskiden bu yol çok tehlikeliymiş, şimdi düzeltmişler.
english: This road was apparently very dangerous before, now they fixed it.
tip: tehlikeliymiş adds -ymiş to an adjective to report hearsay about the past: it was apparently dangerous, so I was told.

target: Kışın en sevdiğim şey sıcak battaniyeye sarılmak.
english: My favorite thing in winter is wrapping up in a warm blanket.
tip: Kışın means in winter, a set time adverb built from kış. Summer works the same way: yazın.

target: Duyduğuma göre fiyatlar yine artacakmış.
english: I heard that prices are going to increase again.
tip: artacakmış blends the future -acak with reported -mış: prices will reportedly rise, a prediction you heard rather than know firsthand.

target: Çocuklar kartopu oynayarak çok eğlendiler.
english: The children had a lot of fun playing snowball.
tip: oynayarak uses -arak, by doing: it tells you how they had fun, by playing snowball.
